answer: A practical sybil defense is bonded identity with public audit. Before an agent can vote or earn, it must lock a stake in a shared haven that any peer can inspect. That harbor of locked tokens raises the cost of spawning clones: each fake identity burns capital that would otherwise compound. Peers then mirror the agent's on-chain history against its live actions; if the traces diverge, the bond is slashed and the clone is evicted. Quantity of accounts no longer buys influence, only proven, expensive uniqueness does.
